text:
jess: quick question — our client tests show inconsistent behavior for the embeddings endpoint when inputs include empty strings and null items. does the API guarantee output order and fixed vector dim for those cases?

samir: order should be preserved (output[i] corresponds to input[i]). vectors are fixed-dim for a given model. which model and SDK call are you using?

jess: using hosted/text-embed-3-small via our python SDK (client.embeddings.create(inputs=...)). example payload:
```json
["hello world", "", null, {\"id\": \"123\", \"text\": \"poke\"}]
```
we saw: one empty string returned non-zero vector, the null produced an error in one run, and the dict entry was shuffled to the end in another run.

linh: thanks for the repro. a few points: 1) null is not a supported input type — server should reject nulls with 400. please convert null -> "" or drop it client-side. 2) dict objects with an id + text are supported (we accept either strings or {id,input} historically). if you send mixed types the SDK normalizer tries to keep order but there was a bug in 2026-02-22 release where batched normalization could reorder object entries when batching split payloads across workers — that was patched yesterday.

mike: for empty strings: the model returns an embedding for the empty token sequence, not an all-zero vector. however some older quantized runtime paths accidentally zeroed the buffer for length==0; that was the bug linh mentioned. confirmed fixed in runtime v1.12.3.

jess: good to know. what's the recommended client-side best practice to avoid surprises?

samir: recommended checklist: 
- canonicalize inputs to either all-strings or all-objects before calling the API (keep order in your array)
- never include nulls; coerce to "" or filter out
- include an explicit id on items if you need stable mapping back to client objects (server preserves array order but ids are more robust)
- if you rely on non-zero empty embeddings, pin runtime >= v1.12.3 or use hosted model flags

jess: thanks. small follow-up: what's the batch size limit and behavior when we exceed it? do we get partial success or hard 413?

linh: current batch token limit for embeddings is 100k tokens per request (sum of tokenized lengths). if you exceed that the request is rejected with 413 Payload Too Large. We do automatic splitting in the SDK for many cases but that can interact with the objects-vs-strings normalization bug (now fixed). If you want atomic behaviour, split client-side and retry with exponential backoff.

mike: also note response shape: always an array of vectors matching input length (for valid inputs). each vector length is the model dimension (e.g., 1536). we never return mixed-length vectors; if anything goes wrong we return an error for that item or the whole request depending on failure mode.

deploy-bot: runtime-service: deployed release v1.12.3 to hosted inference (fix: embeddings empty-input zeroing). :rocket:

jess: perfect — we'll update client normalizer and pin runtime. pinging @product for changelog entry. :thumbsup:

samir: filing a short note in docs/embeddings about null handling and recommended id usage. will drop a link once done.

jess: thanks all!
